correctness.rationale: Over the algebraic closure, split the quadric using u=z+sqrt(c)w, v=z−sqrt(c)w, giving xy=uv. The Segre parametrization converts the cubic to (s_1³+s_1 s_0²)(t_1³+t_1 t_0²)=kappa s_0³t_0³, a fiber product of f(z)=z³+z with kappa/f(z). In characteristic3, their branch values are {infinity} and {0}; otherwise the branch values of f are {infinity,±v_0}, v_0²=−4/27, and those of kappa/f are {0,±kappa/v_0}. These are disjoint iff (27kappa)²≠16. For generic t=1, (27·4)²−16=2^7·7·13; the t substitutions at p=7,13 prevent degeneracy and kappa is nonzero. Disjoint ramification implies the fiber-product divisor is smooth over the algebraic closure; positive intersection of effective (3,3) divisors gives geometric irreducibility. Adjunction yields g=4 and canonical embedding. The nonsplit smooth quadric excludes an F_q-trigonal ruling and hence degrees <=3; the displayed rational point together with Riemann–Roch on K−2P gives a basepoint-free map after removing base divisors of degree at most4. Thus the gonality is exactly4. Independent symbolic Segre and parameter checks, and rational affine/projective smoothness examples at p=3,5,7, corroborate but do not prove geometric smoothness for all q.

value.rationale: This is a uniform constructive answer to a precise genus-four odd-field existence problem, supplying explicit equations and a characteristic-complete smoothness proof rather than relying on finite field enumerations or a heuristic nonsplit-quadric strategy.

final_claim: For each odd q, choose nonsquare c∈F_q and t=2 in characteristic7, t=3 in characteristic13, t=1 otherwise; set kappa=(t^3+t)^2. The two forms Q=xy−z²+cw² and F=y³+x²y+2y(z²+cw²)−kappa x³ intersect in a geometrically smooth, geometrically integral canonical genus-four curve over F_q with F_q-gonality exactly four. The point [1:t²:t:0] is F_q-rational.
